title: Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17, November 2026 data) — 9:15 a.m. ET, the quiet twin: the month-2 print, four days into a possible funding lapse
source: FED: two independent federalreserve.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 — the Board's G.17 announcements feed (feeds/g17.html, HTTP 200, 614,006 bytes) states verbatim "In 2026, the G.17 release on Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization will be published at 9:15 a.m. on January 16, February 18, March 16, April 16, May 15, June 15, July 17, August 18, September 18, October 16, November 17, and December 16", and the Board's own release-date table (releases/g17/release_dates.htm, HTTP 200, 117,098 bytes) carries the row "December 2026 | 16-December-2026" in a maintained table that now runs through July 2027 and still records "October 2025 NA" / "November 2025 NA" from the funding lapse. The same feed additionally publishes the full 2027 schedule ("In 2027 … January 15, February 17, March 15, April 15, May 17, June 16, July 16, August 17, September 16, October 18, November 17, and December 16"), so this date sits inside a two-year forward calendar rather than at its edge. Corroborated a third time by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-12-16 row reads "Retail sales + inventories, Industrial production". PROMOTED from the estimate filed by the industrial-production-2026-11-17 sweep, whose proposal said in its own notes that this id's initial research should promote it on these same two Federal Reserve primaries — this is that session, reading them directly. The Board's verb is "will be published", not the "anticipated" that keeps the Census siblings at estimate. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/industrial-production-2026-12-16.from-industrial-production-2026-11-17.json, now shadowed and inert). Every claim in that proposal was re-derived rather than carried; all survive, and the central one is now measured directly instead of inferred. The reference month is NOVEMBER 2026 — month 2 of the Q4-2026 quarter GDPNow began nowcasting on 2026-10-29 — and that is not an accident of this year: across the 12 December G.17 vintages on record, 11 carry a November reference month, and the single exception (2025-12-03, September data) was produced by a government shutdown. The December edition IS the month-2 edition, structurally. Measured this session against the sibling's own apparatus, re-derived from the Board's 189-date archive joined to ContribArchives (1,871 vintages, 1,822 same-quarter deltas): December G.17 vintages move the GDP nowcast a median 0.1872pp (n=12) against the November-shape class's 0.5833pp (n=12), permutation p=0.0028 — this print's class is measurably ~3x quieter than its own sibling's, and indistinguishable from an ordinary vintage day (p=0.0730 vs the 1,679 non-G.17 vintages). The report's own Equipment channel never reached 0.10pp in any of the 12 (max 0.0661) and PCE outmoved it 12 of 12. On the tape (SPY, 2016-09-07 -> 2026-09-04, baseline n=2,396) the all-G.17 overnight-gap elevation (0.4156% vs 0.2874%, p=0.0016) vanishes in this print's exact class: month-2-with-retail reads 0.2980% at p=0.9052 (n=18), and December G.17 days read 0.4186% at p=0.2207 (n=11). Impact LOW and symbols empty on those measured grounds, not by default; no macro-keyed house playbook exists (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-run 2026-09-06, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. The live variable is PUBLICATION, not the number: PL 119-103 funds through 2026-12-11, so a lapse would begin 00:00 Sat 2026-12-12 and this print sits on day 5 of it — the exposure the November edition's ledger reasoned it was clear of. The confirmed label is a claim about the schedule, and this series demonstrably does not publish when its source agencies stop (2025: two editions cancelled, the 2025-12-16 slot itself folded into 12-23). Three lapses in the archive gave three different outcomes, and the separating variable is BLS: 2013 (16d) delayed the release 11 days, 2018-19 (35d, partial, BLS funded) did not touch it at all, 2025 (43d) deleted two editions. This print's dominant BLS input — the November employment situation, jobs-2026-12-04 — publishes eight days before the cliff. Deliberately NOT proposed alongside it: the 2027-01-15 edition (real, Board-scheduled, dated, but standalone with no known GDPNow vintage — the same grounds on which the November lane declined 09-18 and 10-16), and the 2026 annual revision, which the Board announced 2026-05-15 for "the autumn of 2026" and has still not dated; autumn ends 2026-12-21, five days after this print. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
